description: Coastal Georgia hospitals must comply with ASCE 7-22 wind design requirements; Risk Category IV wind loads apply to all licensed hospitals
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — GA-WIN-001 (Wind Design — Coastal Risk): The structural drawings submitted for Georgia Department of Public Health (DPH) review do not demonstrate that the proposed hospital facility has been designed as a Risk Category IV structure in accordance with ASCE 7-22 Chapter 26 for wind loading, as required for Essential Facilities under the Georgia State Minimum Standard Codes and O.C.G.A. §8-2-20. Hospitals are classified as Essential Facilities (Risk Category IV) and must be designed for the elevated basic wind speeds applicable to their geographic location as mapped in ASCE 7-22 Figure 26.5-1D. For facilities in coastal and near-coastal Georgia counties (Bryan, Brantley, Camden, Charlton, Chatham, Glynn, Liberty, Long, McIntosh), higher design wind speeds and additional wind-borne debris protection requirements apply. The current structural basis of design narrative does not identify the site wind speed, risk category, or compliance path for wind-borne debris region requirements.
fix_template:
1. Revise the structural basis of design to identify the site's basic wind speed from ASCE 7-22 Figure 26.5-1D for Risk Category IV; document the wind speed, exposure category, topographic factor, and all other applicable wind parameters on the structural drawings cover sheet.
2. Confirm the facility is designed as Risk Category IV (Essential Facility) per ASCE 7-22 Table 1.5-1; apply all applicable importance factors and increased design pressures associated with Risk Category IV throughout the structural and envelope design.
3. For projects within the wind-borne debris region (basic wind speed ≥ 130 mph or ≥ 140 mph in hurricane-prone regions per ASCE 7-22 Section 26.12.3), specify impact-resistant glazing or protective shutters for all exterior windows and doors meeting ASTM E1996/E1886; include a glazing schedule noting impact ratings for each product.
4. Provide roof-to-wall and wall-to-foundation continuous load path details on the structural drawings demonstrating complete uplift and lateral load transfer from the roof to the foundation for the design wind event; include connection schedules and calculations.
5. Submit the structural engineer's wind design calculations sealed by a Georgia-licensed Structural Engineer (SE) or Professional Engineer (PE) with demonstrated competency in wind design; submit calculations and signed structural drawings to Georgia DPH Office of Health Planning with the permit application per O.C.G.A. §31-7-1.
code_references: Georgia State Minimum Standard Building Code (IBC 2021 as adopted)

description: Emergency generator must provide 72-hour on-site fuel supply with 10-second automatic transfer per NFPA 110
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — GA-EP-001 (Emergency Power System): The electrical construction documents submitted for Georgia DPH review do not demonstrate compliance with the emergency power supply requirements of Rule 290-9-7-.04 and NFPA 110-2019 for Level 1 systems serving licensed acute care hospitals. Specifically, the fuel storage calculation submitted provides less than 72 hours of on-site fuel at rated generator load, and the automatic transfer switch (ATS) specification does not explicitly confirm a maximum 10-second transfer time from normal power loss to emergency power availability for life safety and critical branch loads. Georgia DPH requires a minimum 72-hour on-site fuel supply and confirmed 10-second transfer for all licensed hospital essential electrical systems. These deficiencies must be corrected before Georgia DPH will issue plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Obtain certified generator fuel consumption data from the manufacturer at rated kW output; calculate required fuel tank volume for 72 continuous hours of operation at rated load; revise fuel tank sizing and include calculations in the permit submittal per Rule 290-9-7-.04 and NFPA 110-2019 Section 7.3.4.
2. Revise the ATS specification to state a maximum 10-second transfer time from loss of normal power to emergency power delivery for all life safety branch loads; include a sequence-of-operations narrative on the electrical drawings per NFPA 70 Article 517 Part III.
3. Provide a complete essential electrical system load schedule separated into life safety, critical, and equipment branches with connected and demand loads; confirm the generator kW rating exceeds the total demand load of all branches simultaneously.
4. Detail secondary containment for all above-ground fuel storage tanks per Georgia EPD requirements; include a spill prevention plan reference and confirm compliance with Georgia Underground Storage Tank regulations (Rule 391-3-15) if any underground tanks are used.
5. Schedule a pre-occupancy generator load bank test with the Georgia DPH Office of Health Planning inspector and submit a test report confirming rated kW output, voltage and frequency stability, and ATS transfer time within 10 seconds before the certificate of occupancy is issued.

description: AII room required in acute care hospitals; minimum negative pressure and 12 ACH total ventilation required
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — GA-INF-001 (Airborne Infection Isolation Room): The construction documents submitted for Georgia DPH review under Rule 290-9-7-.03 do not demonstrate provision of an Airborne Infection Isolation (AII) room that meets the required ventilation parameters for acute care hospitals in Georgia. A minimum of one AII room must be provided with a continuous negative pressure differential of at least -0.01 in. w.g. relative to the adjacent corridor or anteroom, a minimum of 12 total air changes per hour (minimum 2 ACH outdoor air), and HEPA-filtered exhaust discharged directly to the building exterior without recirculation. The submitted mechanical schedules and room data sheets do not confirm these parameters for the designated isolation room(s), and the exhaust discharge location has not been identified on the site plan relative to air intake locations.
fix_template:
1. Clearly designate and label the AII room(s) on the floor plan; provide a room data sheet for each AII room showing negative pressure (-0.01 in. w.g. or greater), minimum 12 total ACH (minimum 2 ACH outdoor air), and HEPA exhaust per Rule 290-9-7-.03 and ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1.
2. Specify HEPA filtration (99.97% minimum efficiency at 0.3 micron) on the exhaust system for all AII rooms; indicate HEPA unit location on the mechanical floor plan and provide a manufacturer's cut sheet with filter efficiency certification.
3. Identify exhaust outlet location on the site plan or building elevation; demonstrate minimum 25-foot horizontal separation from all outdoor air intakes, operable windows, and public pedestrian areas per ASHRAE 170-2021 Section 7.4.
4. Specify a continuous pressure differential monitoring device with a local visual indicator at the room entrance door and a remote audible/visual alarm at the nursing station; connect the monitor output to the BAS with a documented response protocol per FGI 2022 Section 2.2-3.6.
5. Include a start-up and verification test protocol on the mechanical drawings confirming that all AII room pressure, ACH, and filtration parameters will be verified by a qualified testing, adjusting, and balancing (TAB) agency before clinical occupancy; submit TAB report to Georgia DPH with the occupancy application.

description: Operating room minimum 360 SF net; positive pressure relative to corridor with minimum 20 ACH total ventilation
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — GA-SU-001 (Operating Room — Area and Ventilation): The proposed operating room(s) as depicted in the submitted drawings do not satisfy the requirements of Georgia DPH Rule 290-9-7-.03 in one or more of the following areas: (1) minimum net floor area of 360 square feet measured from finished face of wall to finished face of wall exclusive of fixed casework and wall thickness, and/or (2) a minimum of 20 total air changes per hour with positive pressure (+0.01 in. w.g. minimum) relative to the adjacent scrub corridor and all contiguous spaces. The architectural plans do not provide dimensioned room areas with deductions for fixed elements, and the mechanical room data sheets do not confirm the required ACH and pressure relationships for the surgical suite. Both deficiencies must be addressed in the permit submittal to Georgia DPH.
fix_template:
1. Provide a dimensioned floor plan with calculated net area for each operating room; show deductions for fixed casework, built-in equipment, and columns; confirm each OR meets 360 SF net minimum per Rule 290-9-7-.03 and FGI 2022 Section 2.1-3.3.
2. Prepare a pressure relationship diagram for the surgical suite showing all spaces and their relative pressure to adjacent spaces; confirm each OR is positive (+0.01 in. w.g. minimum) relative to the scrub corridor, sub-sterile room, and all adjoining spaces per ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1.
3. Update mechanical room data sheets to confirm a minimum of 20 total ACH for each OR with a minimum of 4 ACH outdoor air; provide engineering calculations demonstrating design airflow volumes meet the minimum ACH at design conditions.
4. Specify ceiling-mounted supply diffusers providing unidirectional (laminar) airflow over the surgical field; diffuser array must encompass at least the operating table footprint plus a 12-inch margin on all sides; include a reflected ceiling plan showing diffuser layout per ASHRAE 170-2021 Section 7.5.
5. Confirm OR temperature (68–75°F) and relative humidity (20–60% RH) control with independent room-level controls; add setpoints to the room data sheet and provide a control sequence of operations narrative in the mechanical specifications.

description: Minimum 100 SF single-bed patient room; maximum 2 beds per room in medical/surgical units
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — GA-PR-001 (Patient Room Size and Configuration): The submitted architectural drawings indicate patient room configurations that do not comply with the requirements of Georgia DPH Rule 290-9-7-.03. Single-bed patient rooms must provide a minimum of 100 square feet of clear floor area measured from finished wall face to finished wall face, excluding the toilet room, closets, and fixed wardrobes. Additionally, Rule 290-9-7-.03 limits patient rooms in medical/surgical units to a maximum of two (2) beds per room; ward-style multi-bed rooms with more than two beds are not permitted in Georgia licensed acute care hospitals. One or more rooms depicted on the submitted drawings fall below the 100 SF minimum or exceed the two-bed maximum configuration.
fix_template:
1. Calculate and tabulate the net clear floor area for each patient room on all nursing units; list each room with its gross dimensions, deductions for toilet room, closets, and fixed elements, and resulting net area; confirm all single-bed rooms meet 100 SF minimum per Rule 290-9-7-.03.
2. Revise the floor plan to eliminate any patient rooms exceeding a two-bed configuration in medical/surgical or general acute care units; provide revised room count and bed count summary for each nursing unit.
3. Show representative room furniture layouts for single-bed and double-bed rooms demonstrating a minimum 3-foot clear path on three sides of each patient bed; confirm the clear path is maintained even with standard furniture in place.
4. Verify that each patient room provides a private toilet room directly accessible from the patient room without requiring the patient to enter the corridor; provide toilet room dimensions showing ADA-compliant clearances per Georgia accessibility requirements (O.C.G.A. §30-3-1 et seq.) and ADA Standards.
5. Confirm exterior window provision per Rule 290-9-7-.03 (windows in patient rooms providing natural light and, where feasible, outdoor views); annotate window sizes and sill heights on the floor plan; confirm minimum glazed area ratios are met.

description: NFPA 101-2021 Life Safety Code adopted statewide for healthcare occupancies; automatic sprinklers required throughout per NFPA 13
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — GA-FLS-001 (Automatic Sprinkler and Life Safety Code Compliance): The fire and life safety documents submitted for Georgia DPH review do not demonstrate full compliance with NFPA 101-2021 Life Safety Code as adopted statewide under O.C.G.A. §31-7-1 and enforced by Georgia DPH for licensed healthcare facilities. Specifically, the fire protection drawings indicate areas within the proposed project scope that lack automatic sprinkler coverage. Georgia licensed hospitals must be fully protected by an automatic sprinkler system designed and installed per NFPA 13-2022 throughout the building, including all closets, corridors, mechanical rooms, ceiling plenums, and interstitial spaces. Additionally, the life safety code compliance plan/code analysis does not address all smoke compartment areas for patient care floors. These omissions must be corrected before Georgia DPH will issue plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Revise fire protection drawings to provide complete automatic sprinkler coverage throughout all project areas, including rooms, corridors, closets, mechanical spaces, and ceiling plenums, per NFPA 101-2021 Section 18.3.5 and NFPA 13-2022; no unsprinklered areas are permitted in a licensed hospital.
2. Provide hydraulic calculations and a water supply analysis for the most hydraulically demanding design area per NFPA 13-2022 Section 19.2; include a water supply test data sheet (test within 12 months) and the hydraulic calculation summary on the fire protection drawings.
3. Revise the life safety code analysis to address smoke compartment layout for all patient care floors; confirm no smoke compartment exceeds 22,500 SF per NFPA 101-2021 Section 18.3.7; show smoke barrier locations, ratings, and door specifications on the floor plans.
4. Specify quick-response sprinkler heads in all patient sleeping rooms and adjacent corridors per NFPA 13-2022; provide a sprinkler head schedule noting response time index (RTI), temperature rating, orifice size, and coverage area for each head type.
5. Coordinate the sprinkler system with the fire alarm system; confirm that the sprinkler system water flow alarm initiates a supervisory signal at the fire alarm control panel and at the local monitoring station per NFPA 72-2022; include a system interface narrative in the fire alarm submittal.

description: Georgia DPH construction permit required before work begins on licensed hospital facilities; submit to Office of Health Planning
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — GA-GEN-001 (Georgia DPH Construction Permit): Construction documents for a licensed acute care hospital in Georgia require prior plan review and approval by the Georgia Department of Public Health, Office of Health Planning, as a condition of the facility's license under O.C.G.A. §31-7-1 and Rule 290-9-7. The submitted application package is incomplete; the required Georgia DPH permit application form, applicable fee, and/or signed and sealed construction documents are missing or deficient. Georgia DPH will not process the permit application until a complete submittal is received. No construction may begin prior to written Georgia DPH approval. Commencement of work without approval constitutes a violation of Rule 290-9-7 and may result in enforcement action by Georgia DPH, including a license sanction against the facility.
fix_template:
1. Complete and submit the Georgia DPH Office of Health Planning permit application, including all required fields; ensure the application is signed by the licensed hospital's authorized representative and the engineer or architect of record per Rule 290-9-7 and O.C.G.A. §31-7-1.
2. Include two (2) complete sets of construction documents bearing the wet or electronic signature and seal of all licensed design professionals of record (architect, structural engineer, mechanical engineer, plumbing engineer, electrical engineer, fire protection engineer) registered in Georgia.
3. Remit the applicable Georgia DPH plan review fee calculated per the current Office of Health Planning fee schedule; attach the payment receipt or fee calculation worksheet to the application.
4. Provide a written project narrative describing the full scope of work, affected licensed categories and beds, estimated construction cost, schedule of construction phases, and proposed infection control measures for work adjacent to occupied patient care areas.
5. Do not authorize contractors to begin construction on the licensed facility premises until written Georgia DPH plan approval is in hand; post the approval letter at the construction site and make it available to Georgia DPH inspectors, local building officials, and the facility's accreditation body upon request.

description: ICRA plan mandatory for all occupied hospital construction; must be filed with the permit application to Georgia DPH
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — GA-INF-002 (Infection Control Risk Assessment — Construction): The permit application submitted to the Georgia Department of Public Health, Office of Health Planning, does not include an Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) plan as required by Rule 290-9-7-.02 for construction and renovation activities in or adjacent to occupied licensed hospital facilities. The scope of work described in the application — including demolition, above-ceiling work, and penetrations of existing walls in proximity to patient care areas — constitutes a Class III or Class IV ICRA risk activity under the APIC classification matrix. An ICRA plan addressing construction barrier type, negative pressure requirements, traffic control, dust and moisture containment, and patient relocation protocols must be submitted to and accepted by Georgia DPH before the construction permit can be issued.
fix_template:
1. Complete the ICRA risk classification matrix (per APIC guidelines or equivalent) for each phase and location of construction activity; determine the activity type (A–D) and patient risk level for each phase; document the completed matrix in the ICRA plan submitted to Georgia DPH per Rule 290-9-7-.02.
2. Develop a written ICRA plan specifying temporary construction barrier type (minimum 0.25-inch drywall for Class III activities or hard-wall isolation for Class IV), barrier installation locations, and provisions for HEPA-filtered negative air machines maintaining negative pressure within the construction zone.
3. Provide a phasing diagram showing the sequence of construction, location of barriers at each phase, contractor entry and egress routes, and debris transport paths that avoid occupied patient care corridors; include tacky mat locations at all construction zone exits.
4. Designate an Infection Control Risk Assessment Officer (ICRAO) responsible for pre-construction walk-throughs, daily barrier inspections, and sign-off on phased construction access; include the ICRAO's name and contact information in the submitted ICRA plan.
5. Establish an on-site daily ICRA inspection log documenting barrier integrity, negative pressure readings at barrier penetrations, and any corrective actions taken; present the completed log to the Georgia DPH inspector during all site inspections and retain records for a minimum of three years per Rule 290-9-7 documentation requirements.
